blocks.title: Attestation, Internal Audits, and Self-Assessments comparison
Attestation, Internal Audits, and Self-Assessments exam shortcuts
items: Formal statement that controls are operating → ATTESTATION
Attestation is a formal confirmation or certification.
Example: Management signs a compliance attestation.
Organization's own audit team performs the review → INTERNAL AUDIT
The work is performed from inside the organization.
Example: Internal audit tests compliance with security policy.
Question asks who oversees audit findings and independence → AUDIT COMMITTEE
The committee provides governance over audit activities.
Example: Board committee reviews unresolved audit findings.
Team evaluates its own controls → SELF-ASSESSMENT
The same organization or owner performs the review.
Example: System owner completes a control checklist.
blocks.example: For audit questions, focus on who performs the review. For penetration testing, focus on the tester's knowledge level and whether reconnaissance touches the target.

questions.q: Management signs a formal statement certifying that required controls are operating as described. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Attestation is a formal statement or certification about controls or compliance.

questions.q: The organization's internal audit department reviews compliance with security policies. What type of audit is this?
questions.explanation: An internal audit is performed by personnel within the organization.

questions.q: A board-level group reviews unresolved audit findings and auditor independence. What is this group?
questions.explanation: An audit committee oversees audit activities, findings, independence, and follow-up.

questions.q: A system owner completes a checklist evaluating the system's own controls. Which assessment is this?
questions.explanation: A self-assessment is performed by the organization or owner evaluating its own controls.
